official.deadline_note: Only applicants who have applied for a Master's degree programme no later than 15 January (summer admission) and 15 September (winter admission) will be considered for a tuition waiver/scholarship. Waiver offers can continue to be issued throughout March, each with a very short acceptance window; the final acceptance deadline is 1 April (summer admission) or 1 November (winter admission).
official.application_cycle: 2027/2028 cycle: summer admission closes 15 January 2027, winter admission closes 15 September 2027
official.status_note: Aarhus University assesses every admission application automatically, so the scholarship round follows the master's admission calendar rather than its own window, and the next summer-admission window opens ahead of the 15 January 2027 deadline.
official.tuition_coverage_note: 'In some cases, the scholarship is a full or partly tuition waiver. In other cases, the tuition waiver includes a monthly grant towards living expenses, typically but not always for the duration of your Master's degree programme.' Faculty of Arts and Aarhus BSS: 'Tuition fee waiver + monthly grant towards living expenses'. Faculty of Natural Sciences and Faculty of Technical Sciences: 'Tuition fee waiver' only.
benefits: Full or partial tuition fee waiver, depending on faculty
Monthly grant towards living expenses at the Faculty of Arts and Aarhus BSS
Where only a tuition waiver is offered, the faculty may assist recipients in searching for a relevant student job
The scholarship offer is delivered together with the letter of admission in the application system
eligibility: Not a citizen of the EU, EEA or Switzerland: 'EU/EEA/Swiss students cannot apply for scholarships at AU'
Liable to pay tuition fees at Aarhus University: 'Scholarships can only be awarded to applicants who are liable to pay tuition fees'
Applied for a Master's degree programme no later than 15 January (summer admission) or 15 September (winter admission)
The scholarship is tied very specifically to your Master's degree programme and cannot be transferred to another degree programme at AU
requirements: Submit the regular admission application by the scholarship deadline
Do not upload any additional documentation: 'You should not upload any additional documentation to your application for admission'
Accept the tuition waiver or scholarship offer within the very short deadline given in the offer letter
If your decision depends on the waiver, do not decline your offer of admission before 1 April (summer admission) or 1 November (winter admission)
documents: No scholarship-specific documents are required or accepted: the admission application file alone is assessed
selection_criteria: Priority is given to applicants with excellent academic qualifications among the academically qualified applicants
Typically only one or two scholarships are offered on each Master's degree programme
At some faculties, strategic focus may be placed on selected degree programmes or applicants from specific countries
Applicants who are not selected receive a tuition fee notification instead of a scholarship offer
coverage: Full or partial tuition fee waiver, depending on faculty
Monthly grant towards living expenses at the Faculty of Arts and Aarhus BSS
No travel, accommodation or insurance coverage is stated
application_method: No separate scholarship application: 'When you apply for admission, your application will automatically be assessed with a view to a possible scholarship along with our academic assessment of your qualifications'
official.application_route: Apply for admission to a specific AU Master's programme in the AU application system by 15 January (or 15 September); the scholarship is assessed inside that same application.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to applicants from outside the EU, EEA and Switzerland who are liable to pay tuition fees
official.international_eligibility: Only applicants from outside the EU, EEA and Switzerland are eligible
official.duration: The duration of the Master's degree programme; the monthly grant is 'typically but not always' for the programme duration
official.description: Aarhus University offers a limited number of Danish state scholarships, financed solely by the Danish state, to the most talented applicants from outside Europe who are liable to pay tuition fees. The award is a full or partial tuition waiver, and at the Faculty of Arts and Aarhus BSS it also carries a monthly grant towards living expenses.
official.program_type: Danish state scholarship administered by the university (tuition fee waiver, with a monthly living-expense grant at some faculties)

verification.notes: Award structure, the four faculty variants, deadlines, selection process and the CPR/NemKonto/tax-card payment mechanics were all confirmed on AU's own pages. AU publishes no monthly grant figure anywhere.

applicant_utility.summary: AU decides this inside your admission application, so the only lever you really control is which faculty and programme you choose, because that determines whether any living-cost money exists at all. Natural Sciences and Technical Sciences waivers come with no monthly grant while Arts and BSS waivers do, so a strong candidate who is indifferent between campuses should read the faculty table before ranking anything. Then plan for the 55% tax withholding that eats the first months of the grant before your Danish tax card arrives.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving non-EU/EEA applicants to the Faculty of Arts or Aarhus BSS, where the waiver is paired with a monthly living grant.
application_readiness_checklist: Read the faculty breakdown first and choose your target faculty deliberately, since it decides whether a living-cost grant exists
File the admission application by 15 January for the September intake; a later application is simply not assessed
Add no extra scholarship documents, because AU states it does not want additional uploads
Keep the offer of admission alive until 1 April (summer) or 1 November (winter) while waivers are still being issued through March
common_rejection_risks: Applying to Natural or Technical Sciences and budgeting as though a monthly grant were coming
Uploading an extra scholarship letter or CV that AU explicitly does not want
Letting the very short acceptance window on a late-March waiver offer lapse
Assuming a waiver follows you if you switch programme, when AU ties it to the specific Master's programme
Declining the admission offer before 1 April while still waiting for a waiver decision
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Settling-in costs such as the room deposit, furniture, a bicycle or a bus card, plus the gap created while 55% of the monthly grant is withheld as tax before a Danish tax card is registered. AU states the scholarship may not cover all living expenses and that it cannot grant further financial assistance.
document_audit: Nothing beyond the admission application is needed for the scholarship itself, so an incomplete admission file is the real document risk
You need a Danish CPR number before you can register a NemKonto, and the grant cannot be paid without an Easy Account
Bring your scholarship letter to the Danish tax centre to get a tax card, otherwise the withholding continues
alerts: The scholarship cannot be transferred to another AU degree programme
If only a tuition waiver is granted you must still show sufficient funds to support yourself for the student residence permit
Scholarship holders from Danish Tax Council-defined developing countries may be exempt from Danish income tax on the grant
Waivers can still arrive during March, so silence in February is not a rejection
Tuition waivers at Natural and Technical Sciences are awarded as 100% waivers to the most qualified and talented students
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: A single admission application in the AU application system, with the waiver decision bundled into the academic assessment and delivered with the admission letter.
